newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Minor selling shakes Pibor vols slightly.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Minor selling shakes Pibor vols slightly.

text.p: Implied volatility of Pibor options traded on MATIF was hanging onto most of its sharp gains made earlier in the week, although cautious selling saw vols dip marginally, traders said on Wednesday.
Pibor volatility has spiked higher in recent days on political worries, as President Jacques Chirac called an election on Monday, 10 months ahead of schedule.

"There has been some selling of June at the higher levels, which is understandable given the speed of the move up," said a trader at a French bank in Paris. "But there is no major downward pressure, and there is unlikely to be until next week."
June Pibor options on the June futures were at 35.0-36.0 percent, after opening at 35.0-40.0 percent, and closing at around 38.5 percent on Tuesday.
June Pibor futures were up four basis points at 96.38 by 1400 GMT, after earlier reaching a high of 96.42.
A trader at a European bank said the level of the put skew was attracting interest with at-the-money 96.40 strike puts trading at about 36.5 percent and 95.90 puts at about 51.0 percent.
"The put skew is so strong that in a trade such as a June one-by-two put spread at the 96.40/95.90 strikes you get good money for it," he said. "Provided you hedge the delta, it should make money."
Delta is the measure of change in the value of the option, compared with the change in the price of the underlying future.
Traders said that investors appeared to be putting on more strategies, and were prepared to take more risks than earlier in the week.
September volatility was at 24.0-26.5 percent, compared with 27.0 percent at the prior close. December and March volatilities were at 21.0/23.0 percent, compared with 23.0 percent previously.
Traders said they were expecting volatility to remain broadly steady until after the weekend, when more information on the likely outcome of the election would be available.
The first poll since the election was called predicted that the ruling centre-right coalition would win 332 seats in the National Assembly, compared with 222 for the combined left-wing opposition.
